draft.title: The origins of Judaism
card: Judaism traces its beginnings to Abraham. Jews believe God made a covenant with him, which is a binding agreement between God and a people.
In the covenant, God promised Abraham many descendants and a land. Abraham is seen as the first ancestor of the Jewish people.
Jews believe God gave the Torah, the teachings and laws, to Moses at Mount Sinai. This came after the Israelites left slavery in Egypt.
Together, the covenant with Abraham and the Torah given to Moses shape how Jews understand where their faith and people began.
draft.remember: Judaism's origins lie in God's covenant with Abraham and the Torah given to Moses at Sinai.

a.q: What is a covenant, as the term is used in Judaism?
opts: A binding agreement between God and a people
A book of laws kept in a synagogue
A festival that marks the escape from Egypt
A leader chosen to teach the community
a.why: A covenant is an agreement between God and a people, first made with Abraham. The Torah is a different thing: it is the teaching Jews believe was given to Moses.
a.clue: Think of what God made with Abraham.

b.q: Which event is linked with Moses in Jewish origins?
opts: Receiving the Torah at Mount Sinai
Receiving the first promise of a land
Becoming the first ancestor of the Jewish people
Making the first covenant with God
b.why: Jews believe Moses received the Torah at Sinai. The promise of land, the role of first ancestor and the first covenant are linked with Abraham, which is the tempting mix-up.
b.clue: Moses and Abraham are tied to different events.

a.best: A binding agreement between God and a people

b.best: Receiving the Torah at Mount Sinai

problems.detail: Why (a) says the covenant was 'first made with Abraham', and why (b) calls Abraham's covenant 'the first covenant'. The Hebrew Bible describes an earlier covenant with Noah (Genesis 9). Abraham's covenant is the first with the ancestors of the Jewish people, so the explanations should say that instead of 'first' alone.
